note: ADishonoredPawn::GameLoad, in full (2012 0x79b360, 964 bytes against retail's 1928). Agent ED had ported it only as far as AActor::GameLoad. Retail adds, over 2012: m_AssociatedActors behind Ar.Ver() >= 17, the prune of m_LatentInteractables whose object or interface is NULL, one packed byte of two retail-only bits (m_bIsControlledByAMatinee, m_bSpecialRootMotionExtract), the two backup matrices and the backup position and rotation. The AActor::GameLoad it starts with is where the player's transform comes back

ADishonoredNPCPawn::GameLoad (2012 0x7c7c40, 1013 against retail's 1488). Retail adds: m_MovableLimbs behind >= 23, m_InitialPossessedRot behind >= 18, m_pStealable / m_pDroppedStealable, a >= 22 block (m_bExpectingPutpocket, m_pMarkedForVanishAction and its timer) and a >= 23 block (m_LastNPCDamageInfo, m_bShadowKilled). Its packed byte carries four bits where 2012's carries three; the fourth is m_bNotifiedFakeDeath, which the 2012 class does not have. A real retail save is version 24, so every gate fires

ADishonoredNPCPawn::IsSaveable: Location == SLL_FILE || bKillDuringLevelTransition (AActor's bit at offset 292 mask 8). Byte-identical to 2012 0x7ab370, so the bit is the same member in both builds. Declared inline in Inc/CppText/ADishonoredNPCPawn.h; without it ShouldLoadObject answers FALSE for the object the stream stops on

ADishonoredNPCPawn's possession block, as GameLoad_Possession: the two script-override references and, behind Ar.Ver() >= 18, m_InitialPossessedRot. 2012 has the two references inline in GameLoad and no rotation

ADishonoredNPCPawn::SeverLimb (2012 0x7c7490): the dead-NPC branch reads its TArray<FName> of joint names and does not sever. Reads no stream bytes

ADishonoredNPCPawn::PostGameLoad (2012 0x7b0fc0): reads no stream bytes, so the empty UObject body is safe. What it costs is that a restored corpse does not enter StateNPCMasterDead_Limp and a restored NPC does not re-grab the movable it was holding
ADishonoredNPCPawn::GameSave (2012 0x7bdb70): not ported and not declared, as ADishonoredPawn::GameSave is not. The writing half of the object layer does not exist in this tree

ADishonoredNPCController::GameLoad - agent EB left this address as a candidate. Confirmed: AActor::GameLoad, then Ar << Pawn (AController::Pawn @584), a virtual with that pawn, UArkComponentContainer::StartAllComponents(m_ComponentContainer @900), Ar << m_pAIBrain (@896), Ar << m_pLastGoToKismetAction (@920) and, behind Ar.Ver() >= 23, Ar << m_pLastShootKismetAction (@924). Every offset lands on a named member. Dictionary record 714 of Dishonored0.sav, so past the player pawn and not on this milestone's path

UProperty::ShouldSerializeValue (2012 0x2fe0): retail's LAST disjunct was missing. A property whose flags carry 0x0002000000000000 is skipped whenever FArchive::ArIsDisSaveLoad is set - an Arkane property flag, declared here as CPF_DisNoSaveGame (the name is ours; property flags are #defines, so no PDB or cooked package names them). The cooked packages set it on hundreds of properties, nineteen of USequenceOp's and USequenceEvent's twenty-six included, so without it every binary property walk in the save read far more bytes than retail wrote

UByteProperty::SerializeItem (2012 0x31da0, byte-identical): its first disjunct is (Ar.GetPortFlags() & PPF_ForceBinarySerialization). Without that flag an enum ByteProperty is read BY NAME, four bytes through the save's string dictionary, where retail wrote one raw byte. Fixed by setting the flag on the two DisSaveLoad load archives, which is where retail's FLevelLoader constructor sets it

USequenceEvent::GameLoad (2012 0x318e60): agent ED's port read only the archetype reference. Retail reads a FLOAT after it - the activation time relative to the clock the event runs on (the bend-time clock unless m_bAlwaysOutOfBendTime, offset 140 mask 0x400) - so a restored event keeps its re-trigger delay in a session whose clock started again. Those four bytes desynchronised the stream at the first Kismet event in it: the value in Dishonored0.sav is -131.767, exactly minus the world clock the same save records
USequenceEvent::GameSave (2012 0x318e10): the same FLOAT, written as ActivationTime minus the clock

FLevelLoader::FLevelLoader, the not-found branch and the port flags. Retail registers an FObjectRef for every dictionary record it did not retry through the package loader - the outer is NULL, or transient, or inside a UWorld - and operator<<(UObject*&) constructs the object when the data stream names it. Agent ED's port took that branch only for a NULL outer, so a runtime-generated Kismet event duplicate inside a resolved sequence (AActor::GeneratedEvents; records 40 and 47 of Dishonored0.sav, which no fresh session has because retail's session generated them by playing) resolved to nothing and stopped the restore. The same constructor ORs PPF_ForceBinarySerialization into its own port flags and the dictionary loader's

FLevelLoader::operator<<(UObject*&): verified against retail, which is where the StaticFindObjectFast / StaticConstructObject pair for a remembered record comes from. Two written additions, because retail cannot reach either case: the record's outer is resolved recursively (a remembered record's outer can be another remembered record), and a record whose outer cannot be resolved at all stops the restore by name instead of raising StaticAllocateObject's "Object is not packaged"

UDishonoredTask_Base::GameLoad - NOT the 2012 body. 2012's 0x727060 is 42 bytes and nothing but the property walk, and it has no entry in match_2012_2013.csv; retail's is 86 and re-reads m_TemplateTaskName after the walk has already read it as a NameProperty, then, behind Ar.Ver() >= 21, m_Description and m_Status, which the walk leaves out because they carry CPF_DisNoSaveGame. Found as one of the only two unnamed retail callers of UObject::SerializeScriptPropertiesBin (the whole exe has five)
UDishonoredTask_Base::GameSave (80 bytes): the same, without the version gate

UDishonoredObjectivesComponent::GameSave / GameLoad, which retail folds onto one body: the objective list, then m_LastTaskID. 42 bytes to 2012's 23 (0x72f800, also unmatched in match_2012_2013.csv). Found as the small retail caller of the TArray<UObject*> serializer immediately after UDishonoredObjective's pair

UDishonoredObjective::GameLoad (2012 0x72f600): agent ED's port had neither the trailing m_TemplateObjectiveName nor the right bits. `2 * b & 0x3E` puts the byte's bits 0..4 on masks 2, 4, 8, 16 and 32 - m_bOptional, m_bCompleteWhenAllTasksComplete, m_bHUDMarkersInitiallyHidden, m_bIsHidden, m_bShowHUDMarkers - and leaves m_bInitiallyHidden out of the stream entirely

UDishonoredGlobalAIManager::GameLoad: agent ED's port stopped after the attention tag and the blackboard reference. Retail reads one more byte behind Ar.Ver() >= 23, into m_bIgnoreIdealMaximumCount (offset 128 mask 2)
